title: Sticky circuit rescue and tenant SLO lease reconciliation hotpatch
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: During a regional failover test we observed a class of "sticky" circuit states where a tenant's circuit stayed open on a subset of nodes because SLO lease renewal metadata was lost during transient control-plane reconvergence. This caused two poor outcomes: (1) recovery attempts kept evicting traffic from the recovering cohort and (2) telemetry showed mismatched SLO ownership leading to incorrect load-shedding decisions. Motivation: quick mitigation for production incidents plus a robust reconciliation path to prevent recurrence. This PR implements a two-part hotpatch: (A) Rescue path in the circuit manager that forces a short idempotent reconciliation handshake between the regional controller and node-local circuit store when a lease renewal is missing for >30s, and (B) SLO lease reconciliation routine that scans owner metadata and repairs mismatched leases with a conservative backoff and audit logging. Design details: - Added CircuitRescue handler in runtime/controller that detects stale circuit-owner gaps and attempts a best-effort rebind. The operation is idempotent and uses a compare-and-swap token to prevent races. - Introduced slo_lease_reconciler service (configurable via feature flag slo.lease_reconcile=true) that runs incremental passes and emits reconciliation metrics slo.reconciliations.total and slo.reconciliations.repaired. Pass logic favors non-disruptive repairs: if tenants show active traffic we issue a soft-binding and keep previous eviction thresholds. - Telemetry: emit audit logs for reconciliations (reconciler.audit) and an event when a circuit is forced-closed by rescue (circuit.rescue.forced_close). - Safety: rescue path uses a per-tenant rate limiter (max 1 repair per 2m) and will not perform eviction or token-bucket resets; it only rebinds owner metadata. - Rollout: feature-flagged and default-disabled. Hotpatch enabled for incident mitigation via feature flag in production for 3 days then evaluated. Backwards compatibility: operates against existing circuit-store schema, no migrations. Checklist: - [x] Rescue handler implemented in runtime/controller - [x] Reconciler service with metrics and audit logs - [x] Unit tests for reconciliation logic and compare-and-swap paths - [x] Integration test simulating lost lease across controller restart - [x] Feature flag and runtime config documented - [x] Observability dashboard queries added to SLO & Incident dashboards (one-liners) Files changed: runtime/circuit/manager.go, controller/slo/reconciler.go, telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml, integration-tests/reconcile_test.go, docs/operational/reconciliation.md Test plan: unit and integration tests included; staged rollout to canary region for 6 hours then global ramp if metrics stable. Related work: follows up on ENG-9182 and previously-reported incident SUP-1287.

review_conversation: Marco Alvarez (reviewer): Can we add a metric to track CAS conflict count so we can detect contention? Requested a small metric and a note in docs.
Ava Chen (author): Added cas.conflicts.count metric and extended docs with expected contention patterns and mitigation. Responded with measurement thresholds in the runbook.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Questioned safety of rebind when tenant is actively sending traffic. Asked for guard that avoids eviction and preserves token buckets.
Ava Chen (author): Confirmed rescue is non-evicting and implemented an explicit guard; added unit test to ensure token-bucket state untouched.
Jonas Müller (reviewer): Asked for CI pass and integration test to simulate controller restart; noted one flaky test on first run.
CI Bot: initial test run failed due to test-flake in reconcile_test.go and lint warning on telemetry naming. Author fixed test timeout and renamed metric to conform; CI rerun passed.
Marco Alvarez: Approved after metrics added and integration test stabilized. Priya approved with no further comments.
release_notes: Hotfix: Add rescue path for sticky circuit states and SLO lease reconciliation to prevent tenants being stuck in recovery. Feature-flagged; disabled by default. Includes non-disruptive repair logic and observability. Recommended to enable in canary region and monitor slo.reconciliations.repaired metric.
testing: Unit tests cover CAS rebind and tenant limiter behavior. Integration test simulates controller restart and missing lease metadata; test validated that traffic is preserved and no token-bucket resets occur. Manual canary plan: enable slo.lease_reconcile=true in canary region, monitor slo.reconciliations.*, cas.conflicts.count, and request success rate for 30m, then ramp to remaining regions. Rollback: disable feature flag and run scripts/rollback_safety_check.sh if unexpected behavior.
notes: This change addresses a latent class of post-failover flaps observed in SUP-1287. Because the rescue path is conservative and feature-flagged, risk is low; metrics added for quick rollback and alerting.
